findings.description: The new no-op loops index reorderedIDs[i] for every fetched item without proving equal lengths. fetchObjectives/fetchKeyResults append duplicate IDs (including overlaps across otherwise advancing pages), but buildReorderedIDs puts specified IDs in a map and omits every fetched occurrence from unused. With fetched items [{"id":"1","position":1},{"id":"1","position":2}] and --ops [{"id":"1","position":1}], buildReorderedIDs returns ["1"]; the first comparison matches and the second evaluates reorderedIDs[1], panicking. This replaces the typed error contract with a process panic before mutation and affects both objective and key-result branches.
findings.evidence: Static hand-trace of exact checkpoint buildReorderedIDs lines 201-255 and no-op loops 398-405 / 433-440. Existing tests cover duplicate user ops but not duplicate backend IDs. No reproducer executed.
findings.requested_change: Reject duplicate/invalid fetched identities with typed invalid_response before replacement/no-op evaluation, and add a regression for overlapping fetched IDs for both levels; ensure the no-op loop cannot index past the derived order.
